attempts.summary: Published node2's HTTP service (port 8080) on node1's management address (10.100.205.10) port 80 using OPNsense NAT: a source-scoped rdr (port-forward) rule restricted to node3 (10.100.205.12), a matching hybrid-mode outbound SNAT rule (rewriting source to node1's LAN IP so node2's flat-L2 replies route back through node1), and an explicit reject filter rule that returns a deterministic TCP RST ("connection refused") for any other source hitting port 80. Also had to stand up the node2 HTTP service itself (busybox httpd via OpenRC, was not pre-existing) and disable OPNsense's built-in port-80 HTTPS-redirect listener/protection which was intercepting port 80 before the NAT rule could apply. Verified end-to-end from node3 (succeeds) and node2/node1-self (refused) both before and after restarting all three nodes one at a time with proof of changed boot identity and post-restart recovery.
